title: Interplay between crystal structure and magnetism in CeCrB$_4$
authors: Mirosław Werwiński, Andrzej Szajek, Andrzej Kowalczyk
abstract: CeCrB$_4$ belongs to the family of MTB$_4$ ternary metal borides, some of whose magnetic phases have recently been identified as quantum spin dimers. Employing density functional theory within the GGA+$U$ framework, this work investigates the key ground-state properties of this system, including its ferromagnetic ground state, the mixed-valence nature of cerium, and the charge transfer from the cationic cerium--chromium layers to the anionic boron layers. In particular, we focus on elucidating the bonding mechanism within the structurally embedded Cr-Cr dimers. Specifically, we evaluate a previously proposed interpretation that the localized Cr $3d_{z^2}$ states are molecular-like bonding and antibonding states. The calculated dependence of the $3d_{z^2}$ electronic structure on the intra-dimer distance correlates with the level-splitting characteristics known for classical homonuclear diatomic molecules.
summary: This work uses DFT to study the electronic and magnetic properties of $	ext{CeCrB}_4$, focusing on the $	ext{Cr–Cr}$ dimer motif. It determines that the material's ground state is ferromagnetic and elucidates that the $	ext{Cr–Cr}$ bonding states behave molecularly. The findings provide insights into how crystal structure dictates magnetic ordering and electronic behavior in these boride compounds.
main_problem: To clarify the molecular nature of localized dimer states in $	ext{MTB}_4$ compounds, determine the magnetic ground state of $	ext{CeCrB}_4$, and resolve the valence state and magnetic moment of Ce.
main_result: The calculations predict that the ferromagnetic (FM) state is the magnetic ground state, and the $	ext{Cr–Cr}$ dimer electronic structure exhibits clear molecular-like bonding and antibonding splitting as a function of inter-dimer distance.
method: Density Functional Theory (DFT) using the GGA+U framework, incorporating fully relativistic calculations and analyzing the electronic density of states (DOS) and magnetic moments.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the $	ext{CeCrB}_4$ crystal structure, which belongs to the $	ext{MTB}_4$ family of ternary metal borides, featuring structurally embedded $	ext{Cr–Cr}$ dimers.
key_observables: Magnetic ground state ($	ext{FM}$ vs. $	ext{AFM}$ energy difference), $	ext{Cr–Cr}$ dimer electronic splitting, $	ext{Ce}$ valence state, and magnetic moments ($\mu_s, \mu_l$).
important_parameters: The Hubbard parameter $U_{4f} = 6 	ext{ eV}$ is used for the $	ext{Ce}$ $4f$ orbitals; the intra-dimer distance $d_{	ext{Cr–Cr}}$ is systematically varied.
main_assumptions: The calculations are subject to DFT limitations, and the $	ext{PBE}+	ext{U}$ correction, while improving the $	ext{Ce}$ $4f$ description, cannot capture all dynamic many-body correlation effects.
figures_summary: Figures show the crystal structure and $	ext{Cr–Cr}$ dimers, and the DOS reveals strong hybridization near the Fermi level, with localized $	ext{Cr}$ states standing out.
paper_structure: The paper systematically investigates the magnetic ground state by comparing $	ext{FM}$ and $	ext{AFM}$ configurations, followed by a detailed electronic structure analysis focusing on the $	ext{Cr–Cr}$ dimer bonding mechanism by varying the inter-dimer distance.
why_interesting: The investigation into localized magnetic moments and the strong correlation effects in the $4f$ electrons of Cerium, combined with the analysis of crystal field splitting in the $	ext{Cr}$ $3d$ orbitals, touches upon correlated electron physics relevant to heavy fermion systems.

figures.caption: Figure 1: CeCrB4 crystallizes in the orthorhombic YCrB4-type structure (space group P bam) with lattice parameters a = 5.942 Å, b = 11.580 Å, and c = 3.496 Å (our experimental data). (a) Single unit cell with the intra-dimer Cr–Cr distances indicated. (b) Antiferromagnetic conﬁguration featuring two magnetically in- equivalent Cr sites, highlighted in diﬀerent colors. The extended projection help to visualise the Cr–Cr dimers within the lattice.

Figure 2: Electronic density of states (DOS) for CeCrB4 in the ferromagnetic conﬁguration: (a) total and site-projected DOS; (b) site-projected Ce and Cr DOS; (c) local Cr 3d orbital con- tributions. The results come from fully relativistic calculations with the magnetization (quantization) axis [001]. The calcula- tions were performed using the FPLO method within the PBE+U approach (U4f = 6 eV).

Figure 3: Electronic band structure of CeCrB4 in the ferromagnetic conﬁguration, presented in a fat-band representation. The local Cr 3d orbital contributions are highlighted in color. The partially ﬂat Cr 3dz2 (m = 0) bands are indicated in magenta and gray for the two respective spin channels. The corresponding high-symmetry points are marked on the enclosed Brillouin zone. The calculations were performed using the fully relativistic FPLO method within the PBE+U approach (U4f = 6 eV).

Figure 5: Electronic density of states (DOS) for CeTB4 com- pounds: (a) local T 3dz2 orbital contributions for T = V, Cr, and Mn (consecutive elements within the 3d series); (b) local 3dz2, 4dz2, and 5dz2 orbital contributions for T = Cr, Mo, and W, re- spectively (three elements belonging to the same group of the periodic table). The calculations were performed using the non- magnetic scalar-relativistic FPLO method within the PBE+U ap- proach (U4f = 6 eV). For all considered compounds, the CeCrB4 structural model was utilized as a template, substituting only the chemical element at the Cr position.

Figure 4: Evolution of the orbital-resolved density of states (DOS) for the Cr 3dz2 (m = 0) state as a function of the intra-dimer dCr–Cr distance in CeCrB4. Individual spectra are vertically shifted by a constant oﬀset for clarity. The vertical dashed line de- notes the Fermi level (E −EF = 0 eV). The spectrum highlighted with a thicker line at 2.40 Å corresponds to the equilibrium conﬁg- uration (eq.). The calculations were performed using the nonmag- netic scalar-relativistic FPLO method within the PBE+U frame- work (U4f = 6 eV). The variation in the interatomic distance dCr–Cr was modeled by scaling the area of the ab plane of the unit cell while keeping the lattice parameter c constant.
